we're aware; I had written several possible fixes.
The issue is a bit complex because there's an interference from the auto-reconnect mechanism.
In order to avoid this issue, for now disable auto-reconnect in Settings > Advanced.
I had written a temptative fix which stops the auto-reconnects if there's a failed connection. But if the failure is from some temporary dns issue, some people would prefer to reconnect.
I'll rediscuss this with other devs to see if we can find some fix.

Thank you for the quick response! Until there is a permanent solution, please consider automatically temporarily disabling auto-reconnect for srt based streams (and maybe show popup warning) after starting the stream.

Any update on this? From my experience, SRT is a major requirement if you want to do affordable and reliable video streaming with OBS over the public internet. What do others use instead of SRT, when they need good reliability across networks with congested peerings / transit between autonomous systems or when streaming over shitty internet connections of hotels for events and so on?

Well, the simplest workaround is to disable auto reconnect in Advanced Settings.
The problem has no easy fix. I offered a solution (see the pr i linked above) but the conundrum is about treating correctly connection errors due to temporary DNS issues.
People in that situation will want to be able to have auto reconnect.

repository.name: obs-studio

_No response_

### OBS Studio Log URL

https://obsproject.com/logs/TSD307e7egWH153z

### OBS Studio Crash Log URL

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

- When streaming to a SRT server which doesn't exist, OBS should not report it has connected
- When stopping streaming (If it was not actually connected) it should stop properly and not get stuck on 'Stopping Streaming...' and also another press of the 'Stopping Streaming...' button should not crash OBS

### Current Behavior

If streaming is started to a non existant SRT server (use any IP, e.g. 127.0.01) it will appear to connect - but then will attempt to reconnect automatically - which OBS then thinks actually connects, but then disconnects. Because of this I believe OBS is stuck in a loop and will always see the connection as successful thus not stopping to auto-reconnect after X tries as per settings.

When clicking 'Stop Streaming' OBS will then get stuck trying to stop it and it will never stop - you can then click 'Stop Streaming...' again and OBS will crash.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure to stream to non existant SRT server, e.g. srt://127.0.0.1
2. Start Streaming
3. You will see OBS looping : Connected, Disconnected, Connecting, Disconnected etc
4. Click 'Stop Stop Streaming'.
5. It will not stop streaming and remains on 'Stopping Streaming...'
6. Click 'Stopping Streaming.....'
7. OBS Will then crash - no crash report made

### Anything else we should know?

_No response_

issue.body:
### Description
This PR is a stand in replacement of the obs-ffmpeg-mpegts output
which currently relies on a pipe to obs-ffmpeg-mux binary.
This improves srt/rist handling.
Additionally this fixes several bugs related to auto-reconnect : 
- auto-reconnect is partially broken with srt & rist; the UI will display a successful reconnect even though it is not the case
because in obs-ffmpeg-mux.c the obs_output_can_begin_data_capture function is not called in the thread doing the reconnect. Fixes: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/issues/6749 
- when non existing urls are used, if auto-reconnect is enabled, obs is locked up.  Fixes: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/issues/5791

### Motivation and Context
Currently srt & rist protocols are supported in obs through their implementations
in FFmpeg/avformat.
It is much preferable to support them natively in obs because this allows for better
logging and easier debugging. We also don't depend on upstream for bug fixes
or for functionalities.
This PR achieves this in the following way:
- it creates an obs-ffmpeg-mpegts muxer separate from obs-ffmpeg-mux project;
The use of obs-ffmpeg-mux allowed for easy support of srt & rist but logging was
an issue.
- it brings the protocol handling in-house by using custom AVIO_Contexts.

Note that the mpegts muxing is still delegated to avformat library.
The mpegts spec is quite complex so it doesn't seem reasonable to do the mpegts
muxing ourselves.
However all the protocol handling is now done in obs itself.

Improvements over the previous srt/rist implementations are the following:
- logging of all protocol stages (opening, writing, closing, failures);
- stats collections (the PR collects stats every 60 seconds; this is not configurable, yet).
The stats inform on the RTT and the link bandwidth (effective bandwidth from obs to ingest)
for srt for instance. The figures can be quite useful for optimization of the stream. They could
also be leveraged for dynamic bitrate.

Further improvements are possible but are dependent on whether a better support of these 
protocols is decided upon by the obs dev team. For instance:
- better customize protocol settings (at the plugin level) and create an UI for that.
- add support for multi-track streaming (audio) (this is mostly at UI level).
- add support for opus codec (requires some UI work in obs Settings).
- support rist multi-destinations (rist can stream to up to 10 ingest points).
- support bonding (link aggregation for srt & rist).

### How Has This Been Tested?
This was tested on windows 10 & macos 10.15.4 against : 
- nimble server,
- wowza server,
- vlc 3 & vlc 4,
- ffplay & ffmpeg.

Works fine.

NOT tested on linux.

TEST builds here: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/actions/runs/2656507203

**Important note on deps**
macos obs-deps require libsrt 1.4.4 and break stats collection with 1.4.1.
The first commit will be dropped once it's merged into master; it enables the right deps which work with this PR.

**CI**
CI is currently broken for various reasons on linux, ~~mac & win~~.
On win: ~~the deps need to ship the import libs of libsrt & librist. This will require an update of obs-deps.~~
On macOS: ~~the deps do not ship the srt & rist dylibs. This will be fixed by the obs-deps PR mentioned above.~~
On ubuntu 18.04, the CI script needs to be updated to manually build libsrt & librist. (The ubuntu version is 
too old to have recent enough packages for srt & rist.)

### Types of changes
- New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- Tweak (non-breaking change to improve existing functionality) 
- Performance enhancement (non-breaking change which improves efficiency)
- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
